newsitem.title: POLAND: Wolczanka plans bond or share issue.
newsitem.headline: Wolczanka plans bond or share issue.

text.p: The Polish garment market Wolczanka SA plans a convertible bond or share issue at the end of this year at the earliest to raise funds for restructuring its production, a Wolczanka deputy president said on Thursday.
"Wolczanka plans to boost its capital through a new share or convertible bonds issue, but no sooner than at the end of the year," Elzbieta Grabska told Reuters.
"We are restructuring our production and we shall see how much we need and, therefore, how big the issue would have to be only in a few months," she said.
She said it was not yet decided if it would be an open or a closed issue.
Grabska said Wolczanka needed funds to market new products which would be sold under a new brand name, a move necessary because of Poland's planned entry into the European Union.

Wolczanka now makes shirts for well known western firms which are sold on EU markets and is concerned that entering those markets under its own brand name could bring an end to such contracts, Grabska said.
Wolczanka's main shareholders are the state-owned PKO BP bank with 22.3 percent, Bank Handlowy SA with 13.1 percent. It has a total of 2.1 million shares.
Its net profit in 1996 was 5.6 million zlotys against 6.5 million in 1995 on sales of 87.9 million and 77.6 million zloty respectively.
